purpose: Mefenamic acid is used to relieve mild to moderate pain, such as headaches, toothaches, muscle aches, and period pain. It is especially helpful for reducing painful menstrual cramps and the heavy bleeding that can come with periods. It works best when taken at the first sign of pain.
how_it_works: Your body makes certain chemicals called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling, and inflammation. Mefenamic acid blocks the enzymes that produce these chemicals, so less pain and swelling occurs. Think of it as turning down the volume on your body's pain signals.
common_side_effects: Upset stomach, nausea, diarrhea, or indigestion are the most common issues. Some people may feel dizzy or get a headache. Taking it with food or milk can help reduce stomach discomfort.
warnings: Do not take this medicine if you have a history of stomach ulcers, kidney or liver problems, or heart disease. Avoid it if you are allergic to aspirin or other NSAIDs. Do not use it for more than 7 days unless your doctor tells you to. It should not be taken during the last 3 months of pregnancy. Stop taking it and contact your doctor if you notice black or tarry stools, which could mean stomach bleeding.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 500 mg to start, then 250 mg every 6 hours as needed with food. It is generally not recommended for children under 14 years old. Always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions and do not exceed the recommended dose.
